text: The destination is not guaranteed to match the source at any point while the sync runs, including while paused. Call commit to reach a matching state; at COMMITTING mongosync takes the commit timestamp (time of the latest source operation) and applies events up to it. (high confidence)

For total size of 64 GB or less migrating to a destination with 4 or fewer CPUs, the copy phase issues fewer concurrent writes. Set an explicit load level at start or restart to override. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

canCommit is true only when the initial sync is complete, the embedded verifier is ready, and lag for mongosync and the verifier is 30 seconds or less (30-second rule from 1.21). lagTimeSeconds is deprecated in 1.21; use lag.overallLagSeconds. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

mongosync is stateless and keeps restart metadata on the destination. After an outage, restart with the same parameters and confirm /progress returns state RUNNING. If the source outage exceeds the oplog window, mongosync cannot resume and the migration restarts from scratch, wiping migrated data. (medium confidence)

Avoid DDL, rolling index builds, an enabled balancer, and moveChunk/moveRange/movePrimary during the sync. DDL raises failure risk; a balancer enabled after start makes mongosync fail. (medium confidence)

mongosync combines and reorders writes during the sync, so for a given document the number of writes on the destination can differ from the source. Documents are inserted in undefined order, not source natural order. (high confidence)

mongosync runs two phases in order: collection copy (initial transfer, by splitting source collections into partitions) and then change event application (CEA), which starts after the copy ends. (high confidence)
CEA opens a change stream on the source and applies events to the destination. It applies events received during the copy phase first, then events received during CEA. (medium confidence)

Do not send application reads or writes to the destination until commit has run and /progress shows canWrite true. Do not use mongosync to maintain a standing secondary for DR or analytics. (high confidence)

Read /progress to see the phase: info is "collection copy", "change event application", "waiting for commit to complete" or "commit completed". collectionCopy.estimatedCopiedBytes is per instance; sum it across instances and divide by estimatedTotalBytes for percent complete. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

During the copy, unique indexes sync as non-unique, TTL indexes get expireAfterSeconds set to MAX_INT, hidden indexes sync as non-hidden, and capped collections get the maximum size. These revert during COMMIT. On source 6.0+ (or buildIndexes afterDataCopy) indexes build after the data copy. (medium confidence)
Transactions might not appear atomically on the destination, and retryable writes may not be retryable there. (low confidence)
